bibliographic.title: An assets-liabilities dynamical model of banking system and systemic risk governance
bibliographic.citation_apa: Fatone, L., & Mariani, F. (2019). An assets-liabilities dynamical model of banking system and systemic risk governance. arXiv preprint arXiv:1905.12431.

methodology.method_family: stochastic differential equations, optimal control, statistical simulation
methodology.study_design: mathematical dynamical model with numerical simulation of systemic risk governance
methodology.sample_description: homogeneous population of banks represented by assets and liabilities in a dynamical banking system model
methodology.technology_context: assets-liabilities dynamical model of banking system with monetary authority intervention and cooperation mechanism among banks

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The paper addresses mathematical systemic risk governance in a banking dynamical model using stochastic differential equations and optimal control; it does not discuss LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the text repeatedly uses governance and banking in a regulated financial context, the study concerns probabilistic control of bank failures in a stochastic assets-liabilities model. There is no mention of large language models, conversational AI, human oversight of AI outputs, guardrails, observability, or related generative-AI governance mechanisms relevant to the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is explicit from title, abstract, and introduction; no ambiguous overlap with conversational LLM governance.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based only on front matter and introduction pages provided. Internal methodological clarity appears adequate for a mathematical finance modeling paper, but ethics, limitations, and full results are not visible in the excerpt. Appraisal does not imply eligibility for the conversational LLM governance review.

cerqual.explanation: For the target review on conversational governance of LLM-based systems, this preprint has no evident relevance despite strong internal coherence as a banking systemic-risk modeling study.

coding.theme: Systemic risk governance in banking dynamical models
coding.subtheme: Optimal control of failure probability via ideal-bank reference behavior

synthesis.main_claim: Systemic risk in a homogeneous banking population can be governed by keeping the probability of widespread bank failure within bounds through monetary-authority choices for an ideal bank and cooperation rules derived from a stochastic optimal control problem.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes and illustrates a generalized assets-liabilities dynamical banking model with cooperation and direct monetary authority intervention, plus a governance method using pseudo mean field approximation and numerical shock simulations.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence for conversational LLM governance; at most peripheral contextual background on the word governance in banking risk modeling, not on AI or conversational systems.

evidence.claim: Paper is a 2019 arXiv preprint on banking systemic risk, not LLM or conversational AI.

evidence.claim: Study objective is governing systemic risk in a banking dynamical model.
evidence.excerpt: We consider the problem of governing systemic risk in an assets-liabilities dynamical model of banking system.

evidence.claim: Governance means controlling probability of systemic bank failure, not AI oversight.
evidence.excerpt: The systemic risk governance pursues the goal of keeping the probability of systemic risk in a bounded time interval between two given thresholds.

evidence.claim: Monetary authority implements governance through ideal-bank rules and cooperation mechanism.
evidence.excerpt: The monetary authority is responsible for the systemic risk governance.

evidence.claim: Method uses stochastic differential equations and optimal control.
evidence.excerpt: These rules are obtained solving an optimal control problem for the pseudo mean field approximation of the banking system model.

evidence.claim: Empirical evaluation is numerical simulation with shocks, not field study of AI systems.
evidence.excerpt: Numerical examples of systemic risk governance in presence and in absence of shocks acting on the banking system are studied.
We limit our attention to the modeling of systemic risk in banking systems.
